name: Henadad
title: Levitical builder in Jerusalem
summary: Henadad was the head of a Levitical family that played an important role in the rebuilding of Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile. His descendants actively participated in building the walls of Jerusalem under Nehemiah and in temple service. The family is mentioned several times in Ezra and Nehemiah as faithful servants in the restoration work.

keyEvents.title: Descendants' participation in the foundation of the temple
keyEvents.description: The sons of Henadad were among the Levites who supervised the work on God's house when the temple was rebuilt under Zerubbabel.

keyEvents.title: Binnui repairs Jerusalem's wall
keyEvents.description: Binnui, son of Henadad, repaired a section of Jerusalem's wall under Nehemiah's leadership.

keyEvents.title: Bavvai, son of Henadad, builds on the wall
keyEvents.description: Another descendant of Henadad participated in the repair work on another section of Jerusalem's wall.

keyEvents.title: The Levites Seal the Covenant
keyEvents.description: Descendants of Henadad were among the Levites who sealed the covenant to follow God's law during Nehemiah's reforms.

keyEvents.title: Supervision of Temple Work
keyEvents.description: Kadmiel and the sons of Henadad stood with their sons and brothers to supervise the workers at God's house.
